title: Complaints about modern dance bands, saxophones and electric guitars
summary: Barnes says old dances were far better than today's, complains about youngsters, too many saxophones and guitars with microphones.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: About a half an hour. Well I tell you, in them days, it was a hundred percent better than it is now. You can take what you want and do what you want. I say it is better than you go now. Now they start the dance at ten o'clock. Sometimes eleven o'clock. Two, three o'clock is over. You take a bunch of people, go somewhere to get drunk, get snotty, and some change your mind, well there ain't nothing. See there ain't nothing. You take the music they play, now it's all the same music. This is what we play, this is what we play, this is what we play, this is what we play. But after I got mixed up, me and myself, and played with a couple of our band there, and wrap it up and put it on the side.
Yeah, but we're playing with that kind of band.

No, I put it on the side, I don't want to be bothered, not at all. Because I tried it a couple of times, and each time I met them, I met them youngsters on the end. And they used to play with that band, and they couldn't play what you were playing, you couldn't play what they play. Oh man. Then they're blowing all kinds of notes, and anything goes. Oh man. I said to myself, I said, well, before I lose my heart, I'm going to lose the tone of it, or something I'll even say there.
They used a lot of saxes in those bands, too, weren't they?

Yeah, there's so many saxes, and everybody playing saxes. I remember a time when you buy the instruments, you got tired of it, and you pull your lungs, you throw it away. But now everybody buying an instrument, keep it, and all you got to do is blow it. That's all, you got to blow it. Get the guitar the same way, you get one string on the guitar, you can play it. You can play it with a joke. Ding, ding, ding, down, pull, pull, oh, oh. That's nothing new, you know. Now, I don't know what to say about it or what to make about it.
Your biggest band is today. Get your mic and holler. And I sing. Holler. You get back in there. Yeah. One kind of guitar. Yeah. Yeah.
Electric guitars make a lot of noise. Oh, man.
